newsitem.title: UK: Soccer's UK Hall of Fame seeks to float on AIM.
newsitem.headline: Soccer's UK Hall of Fame seeks to float on AIM.

text.p: Soccer exhibition operator Hall of Fame Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it is planning a June float on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) and will use the proceeds to develop its site in the Pepsi Trocadero in London's Piccadilly area.

The company plans to build and manage a Hall of Fame exhibition for British soccer, where visitors will be able to experience a multi-media presentation about the current game and history of soccer in Britain.

The exhibition will include, amongst other features, 'The Tunnel Experience' where the visitor will be treated to an audio-visual representation of a stadium tunnel in order to prepare him or her for the exhibition and 'The Premiership Hall of Fame', intended to be the highlight of the visit.

Twelve initial inductees will be voted into the Premiership Hall of Fame by a committee which will put forward a list of players and will be chosen based on the footballer's achievements and standing in the game.
Directors said they were confident that this could become a televised event.

Hall of Fame, which is chaired by England 1966 World Cup hero Geoff Hurst, seeks to raise about 3.7 million stg, after expenses, and will have a market capitalisation of around 5.2 million stg at the issue price of 10p per share.
The placing involves the sale of shares in units which are being placed at 50p each. A unit will represent five ordinary 10p shares and one warrant.
Dealings in the shares and warrants are expected to begin on June 13.
